modules.name: core
modules.title: Platform Core Ontology
modules.description: Upper module for the application platform ontology: principals, resources, events, and XACML-style policy architecture roles. All domain modules import this module. Since 0.2.0: tenants (the platform itself being a distinguished tenant), capabilities, tenant-owned applications, and the closed delivery-channel vocabulary — platform-wide primitives promoted from the control-plane module while all terms are draft. Since 0.5.0: the decision point and the enforcement point are disjoint — a decision is rendered by one component and acted on by another (P13).
modules.blurb: Upper module: principals, tenancy, capabilities, applications, authorized parties, delivery channels and the XACML roles.

modules.name: authn
modules.title: Authentication Module
modules.description: Credentials, authentication events and methods, identity providers, and NIST SP 800-63 assurance levels (modelled as SKOS concepts with numeric ranks for comparison). Since 0.2.0: authentication journeys — governed definitions per delivery channel, and executions comprising the events a principal actually traversed; achieved assurance lives on the execution. Since 0.3.0: proof-of-possession keys, the confirmation binding of RFC 7800 as used by DPoP (RFC 9449), which sender-constrains sessions and tokens so a stolen artifact is useless without the private key.
modules.blurb: Credentials, identity providers, assurance levels, authentication journeys and issuer-scoped subject identifiers.

modules.name: session
modules.title: Session Module
modules.description: Sessions, tokens, lifecycle states, and the binding between a session and its originating authentication. Since 0.2.0 sessions are established by an authentication journey EXECUTION rather than a single event (a structural retarget performed while all terms are draft); step-up elevations are further executions on the same session, and the effective AAL is the latest successful execution's. Since 0.3.0: session handles — the opaque value a cookie carries — and DPoP-style sender constraining, so a handle identifies a session while the proof-of-possession key authenticates the presenter.
modules.blurb: Sessions established by journey executions, step-up elevations, and tokens carrying both ends of their journey.

modules.name: ingress
modules.title: Ingress Module
modules.description: Gateways, listeners, routes, TLS termination, and upstream services. Deliberately implementation-independent: the terms describe the network entry model itself, not any particular gateway product or API. Since 0.2.0: route matching by domain and path, and the binding from a route to the tenant it serves — the configuration from which ingress resolves tenant context, and therefore the root of tenant.access. Since 0.3.0: the application a route serves, which completes the route as an application access endpoint.
modules.blurb: Network entry: gateways, listeners, routes, TLS termination and upstream services — deliberately implementation-independent.

modules.name: authz
modules.title: Authorization Module
modules.description: ABAC-first authorization: policies, rules, attribute assertions with provenance, roles, decisions, and obligations. Vocabulary aligns to XACML architecture. Since 0.2.0: the closed, platform-owned entitlement dimension scheme and entitlement grants (machine-generated projections of upstream governance, distributed to ingress), plus ingress admission decisions. A grant is a conferral with lifecycle and derivation — distinct from an attribute assertion, which is an observation.
modules.blurb: ABAC-first authorization plus the platform-owned coarse-grained layer: dimensions, grants, actions and admission decisions.

modules.name: control-plane
modules.title: Control Plane Module
modules.description: Control plane components, administrative scopes, and meta-authorization: policy/config change events and their human approvals. Encodes the 'agents execute, humans authorize' invariant, with management vs. capability control planes separating governance from actuation. Since 0.3.0: the scope tree with locality and scope-dependent approval rigor; capability subscriptions, bundles, hard dependencies, and per-scope offerings (no cross-scope parity); application enablement, observed-then-confirmed capability requirements, and portals. Tenant and Capability were promoted to core in this version, while draft.
modules.blurb: Two-tier planes, the scope tree, and the chain from subscriptions and offerings to declarations and mutations.

modules.name: commitment
modules.title: Commitment Module
modules.description: Non-functional commitments a capability offering carries — one metric, a target with unit and comparator over a window, a measurement source and a validation mechanism — and the windowed observations that evidence them. A sibling of the identity modules: it imports core and control-plane and nothing imports it. Vocabulary from specifications: SOSA/SSN for observable properties and observations, QUDT for units. Scaffolded at 0.1.0 (D58) with one competency question; measurements never enter per-request. Since 0.2.0: a commitment is a desired-state declaration (D59) — it is declared through the management plane, bound to a scope that contains its offering's scope, approved where the scope requires it, and superseded rather than edited.
modules.blurb: Non-functional commitments on offerings — metric, target, window, measurement source, validation — and the windowed observations that evidence them. A sibling module; nothing imports it.

terms.name: Application
terms.definition: An independently developed application owned by exactly one tenant, reachable through ingress once enabled, and consuming platform capabilities per its confirmed requirements.
terms.editorialNote: What a subject may do inside the application is application-owned (Level 3) and deliberately out of this ontology's scope.

constraints.message: An application must be owned by exactly one tenant (the platform tenant for platform-owned applications).

terms.name: BusinessClient
terms.label: Business client
terms.definition: A party holding a business relationship with the firm — the firm's customer, retail or corporate. A business client is not itself authenticable; principals act for it, which is what lets one corporate client have many users and one person hold both a staff identity and a client relationship.
terms.editorialNote: This is the word 'client' in its business sense, and the ontology reserves it for that meaning alone. The OAuth client registration is a different and unrelated thing — see authn:OAuthClientRegistration.

constraints.message: A business client must carry exactly one canonical customer identifier.
Business client has no principal acting for it — a relationship nobody can exercise; route to stewardship review.

terms.name: Capability
terms.definition: A platform offering provided to tenants via subscription. Each capability is governed by exactly one capability control plane.

constraints.message: Capability participates in a circular capability dependency — hard dependencies must form a DAG.

terms.name: DeliveryChannel
terms.definition: The delivery avenue through which platform capabilities are consumed, never a self-asserted claim. For interactive sessions it follows from the session's device class. Members are individuals in a closed, platform-owned scheme.

vocabulary.label: AI agent
vocabulary.note: Delegation semantics deliberately deferred; see the agent-channel backlog questions.

terms.name: HumanPrincipal
terms.definition: A principal representing a human user, identified via the firm's directory (e.g., SID/HR identifier).

terms.name: PlatformEvent
terms.definition: An auditable occurrence on the platform. Subclassed by domain modules (AuthenticationEvent, PolicyDecision, PolicyChangeEvent).

constraints.message: Every platform event must have exactly one occurrence timestamp.
performedBy must reference a Principal.

terms.name: PlatformTenant
terms.definition: The distinguished singleton tenant representing the platform itself. Platform-owned applications are owned by it, and it holds capability subscriptions like any tenant, keeping every ownership and coverage rule uniform. Exactly one individual is expected (stewardship-enforced).

terms.name: PolicyAdministrationPoint
terms.definition: Component through which policy is authored and managed (XACML PAP).

terms.name: PolicyDecisionPoint
terms.definition: Component that evaluates policy and renders authorization decisions (XACML PDP).

terms.name: PolicyEnforcementPoint
terms.definition: Component that intercepts access and enforces PDP decisions (XACML PEP).

terms.name: PolicyInformationPoint
terms.definition: Component that supplies attribute values used in policy evaluation (XACML PIP).

terms.name: Principal
terms.definition: An entity that can be authenticated and to which authorization decisions apply.

constraints.message: Every principal must carry exactly one canonical firm-wide identifier.

terms.name: Resource
terms.definition: Anything access to which is governed by policy: services, routes, data assets, control-plane operations.

constraints.message: Resource has no governing policy — flag for stewardship review.

terms.name: Tenant
terms.definition: An organizational unit onboarded to the platform, to which subscriptions, applications, entitlement grants, and data planes are scoped.

terms.name: WorkloadPrincipal
terms.definition: A principal representing a non-human workload (service, agent, job), identified via a workload identity such as a SPIFFE ID.

terms.name: displayName
terms.definition: Human-readable label for governance and stewardship UIs.

terms.name: identifier
terms.definition: The canonical identifier for this entity in the firm's registry for its kind — a SPIFFE ID, a directory identifier, a customer identifier, a device registration.

terms.name: occurredAtTime
terms.definition: Timestamp at which a platform event occurred.

terms.name: validFrom
terms.definition: Start of a validity window (attribute assertions, subscriptions, subject identifiers). Promoted from authz while draft — generic temporal vocabulary belongs in the upper module.

terms.name: validUntil
terms.definition: End of a validity window.

terms.name: actsForClient
terms.definition: Business client a principal acts for. Retail relationships are typically one principal to one client; corporate relationships many principals to one.
terms.editorialNote: Distinct from tenant membership. Whether a business client is ever also a tenant is deliberately left open.

terms.name: enforcedBy
terms.definition: Links a resource or route to the policy enforcement point that mediates access to it.

terms.name: governedBy
terms.definition: Links a resource to a policy that governs access to it.

terms.name: hasActingIdentity
terms.definition: Principal under whose identity a resource acts — a control plane component's SPIFFE workload identity, for example. Resources cannot be principals; their acts are performed by this principal. Promoted from control-plane while draft.

terms.name: ownedBy
terms.definition: Tenant that owns an application or portal — exactly one (enforced in SHACL); ownership transfer is a supersession of declarations, never co-ownership. Platform assets are owned by the distinguished platform tenant.

terms.name: performedBy
terms.definition: Links a platform event to the principal that performed it. Typing enforced in SHACL, not via rdfs:domain/range.

terms.name: targetsResource
terms.definition: Links an event or policy to the resource it concerns.

terms.name: AssuranceLevel
terms.definition: NIST SP 800-63 assurance level (IAL/AAL/FAL), modelled as an individual with an integer rank for ordering in SHACL-SPARQL constraints.

terms.name: AuthenticationEvent
terms.definition: A discrete attempt (successful or failed) to authenticate a principal.

constraints.message: An authentication event must concern exactly one principal.
An authentication event must record at least one authentication method from the controlled vocabulary.
An authentication event must record whether it succeeded.
A successful authentication event must record an achieved assurance level.

terms.name: AuthenticationJourneyDefinition
terms.definition: A governed template of an authentication flow (e.g., 'web-default: password then OTP, yields AAL2'), bound to the delivery channels it serves. Changes to definitions are security-relevant desired state and flow through the control plane's declaration and approval machinery.

terms.name: AuthenticationJourneyExecution
terms.definition: A principal's concrete traversal of a journey definition, comprising the authentication events actually performed. Achieved assurance is a property of the completed flow, not of any single step.

constraints.message: A journey execution must comprise at least one authentication event.
A journey execution must concern exactly one principal.
A journey execution must record whether it succeeded.
Journey execution follows no governed definition — an ungoverned authentication path, and a session whose channel cannot be established.
A successful journey execution must record an achieved assurance level.

terms.name: AuthenticationMethod
terms.definition: A controlled-vocabulary concept for how authentication was performed. Members are individuals, not subclasses.

terms.name: Credential
terms.definition: An artifact used to prove an identity claim (password record, FIDO2 key registration, client certificate, workload SVID).

constraints.message: A credential must be bound to a principal.
A credential must have an issuing identity provider.

terms.name: IdentityProvider
terms.definition: A system that asserts principal identities (enterprise IdP, workload identity issuer).

terms.name: OAuthClientRegistration
terms.label: OAuth client registration
terms.definition: The registration through which the platform obtains tokens from an identity provider, held by the session manager, one per audience.
terms.editorialNote: Protocol bookkeeping, deliberately thin. Its client_id identifies the registration and nothing else — no tenancy, no channel, no caller identity — and is derivable from the audience. Entitlement decisions must never be made from it. The firm's customer is core:BusinessClient.

constraints.message: An OAuth client registration must carry exactly one client_id.
An OAuth client registration must be held at exactly one identity provider.
An OAuth client registration serves at most one audience — the platform maintains one registration per audience.

terms.name: ProofOfPossessionKey
terms.label: Proof-of-possession key
terms.definition: The public half of a key pair whose private half the presenting software proves possession of per request, sender-constraining the session or token bound to it.
terms.editorialNote: DPoP (RFC 9449) with the confirmation claim of RFC 7800. Distinct from a credential: presenter-generated rather than issuer-issued, and proving continuity of possession rather than an identity claim.

constraints.message: A proof-of-possession key must carry exactly one JWK thumbprint — it is what a presented proof is compared against.

terms.name: SubjectIdentifier
terms.definition: A naming fact: at one issuer, one subject value denotes one principal (RFC 9493 / OIDC sub). Read in reverse at resolution time — a token or security event carries the subject, and this yields the principal.

constraints.message: A subject identifier must carry exactly one subject value.
A subject identifier must be scoped to exactly one issuer.
A subject identifier must denote exactly one principal.
A subject identifier must name its RFC 9493 format.
Same issuer and subject value denote more than one principal — subject-identifier collision.

terms.name: SubjectIdentifierFormat
terms.definition: RFC 9493 subject identifier format; members are individuals in a closed scheme, extended by MINOR bump.

vocabulary.label: email
vocabulary.note: Email subjects are recyclable by issuers — validity windows matter most here.

terms.name: assuranceRank
terms.definition: Integer rank of an assurance level, used for ordered comparison in constraints (AAL1=1, AAL2=2, AAL3=3).

terms.name: clientId
terms.definition: The client_id of an OAuth client registration — a protocol identifier, not a platform-semantic one.

terms.name: keyAlgorithm
terms.definition: Signature algorithm the proof-of-possession key is used with (for example ES256).

terms.name: keyThumbprint
terms.definition: JWK SHA-256 thumbprint identifying a proof-of-possession key (RFC 7638) — the jkt value a confirmation claim carries. Identifies the key without disclosing it, and is what an enforcement point compares a presented proof against.

terms.name: subjectValue
terms.definition: The subject string as the issuer mints it (the sub claim value, an email, an opaque handle).

terms.name: succeeded
terms.definition: Whether the authentication event or journey execution succeeded.

terms.name: achievedAssuranceLevel
terms.definition: AAL achieved by a successful authentication event or journey execution. For executions, this is the flow's outcome — password alone achieves nothing; password+OTP achieves AAL2.

terms.name: atIssuer
terms.definition: Identity provider within whose namespace a subject identifier is unique.

terms.name: authenticatedPrincipal
terms.definition: The principal that the authentication event concerns.

terms.name: comprisesEvent
terms.definition: Authentication event that is a step of a journey execution. Single-step flows (passkey, client credentials) are one-event executions.

terms.name: confirmedByKey
terms.definition: Proof-of-possession key a session or token is sender-constrained to — the cnf binding of RFC 7800, carried as cnf.jkt under DPoP. A session or token without one is a bearer artifact: whoever holds it can use it.

terms.name: credentialOf
terms.definition: Principal to which a credential is bound.

terms.name: followsDefinition
terms.definition: Journey definition a journey execution traversed. Mandatory (SHACL): the definition states the channel it serves, so a session with no definition behind it has no established channel and no governed authentication path.

terms.name: forAudience
terms.definition: Audience an OAuth client registration obtains tokens for. The platform maintains one registration per audience.

terms.name: identifierFormat
terms.definition: RFC 9493 format of a subject identifier.

terms.name: identifies
terms.definition: Principal a subject identifier denotes. One (issuer, value, party-scope) combination must never identify two principals (collision invariant, SHACL); one principal may hold several identifiers, even at one issuer (linking, migration).

terms.name: issuedBy
terms.definition: Identity provider that issued a credential or asserted an identity.

terms.name: registeredWith
terms.definition: Identity provider an OAuth client registration is held at.

terms.name: servesChannel
terms.definition: Delivery channel a journey definition serves. This is what establishes a session's channel, for every channel — a client-credentials definition serves api, a passkey definition serves web — so the derivation does not depend on the session having a device.

terms.name: usedCredential
terms.definition: Credential presented in an authentication event.

terms.name: usedMethod
terms.definition: Authentication method concept used in an authentication event.

terms.name: AccessToken
terms.definition: Token presented to resource servers to authorize requests (e.g., OAuth 2.0 access token).

terms.name: Device
terms.definition: The requesting client a principal holds a session on, identified in the firm's registry and the unit of session identity: the platform issues one session per principal per device. Non-interactive callers have no device.

constraints.message: A device must carry exactly one identifier — a concurrency limit counts sessions per device, and an unnamed device cannot be counted.
A device must have exactly one device class from the closed vocabulary — concurrency limits are configured against it.

terms.name: DeviceClass
terms.definition: The kind of requesting client a session runs on — browser or mobile — as a closed vocabulary. It classifies the client software rather than the hardware or operating system, and corroborates the channel its journey definition establishes. Concurrency limits are configured per device class.

terms.name: IDToken
terms.definition: OIDC ID token asserting the authentication of a principal.

terms.name: RefreshToken
terms.definition: Token exchanged for new access tokens without re-authentication.

terms.name: Session
terms.definition: A bounded period of authenticated interaction between a principal and the platform, established by an authentication event.

constraints.message: Every session must be established by exactly one authentication journey execution (single-step flows are one-event executions).
Session elevations must be authentication journey executions.
Every session must be bound to exactly one principal.
Every session must have exactly one lifecycle state.
Every session must have an expiry.
Session principal must match the principal of its originating authentication event.
An active session must originate from a successful authentication journey execution.
A session runs on at most one device; non-interactive sessions have none.
Principal holds more than one active session on the same device — the platform issues one session per user per device.
Principal exceeds the configured concurrent-session limit for this device class.
Session's device class implies a different channel than its journey definition establishes.
Session is not sender-constrained: no proof-of-possession key confirms it, so a stolen handle alone would be replayable.
Session issued a token bound to a different key, or to no key at all — sender constraining must not be lost at token issuance.
One proof-of-possession key confirms sessions bound to different principals — key confusion.

terms.name: SessionHandle
terms.definition: The opaque value presented to identify a session, typically carried in a cookie. It identifies but does not authenticate; several handles may resolve to one session across rotations.

constraints.message: A session handle must resolve to exactly one session — an ambiguous handle is a session-fixation hazard.

terms.name: SessionState
terms.definition: Lifecycle state of a session; members are individuals (Active, Expired, Revoked, Suspended) rather than subclasses.

terms.name: Token
terms.definition: A signed artifact carrying claims, issued within a session.

constraints.message: Every token must have an expiry.

terms.name: expiresAt
terms.definition: Instant at which the session or token expires.

terms.name: notBefore
terms.definition: Instant before which the session or token is not valid.

terms.name: boundToPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal to which the session is bound.

terms.name: elevatedBy
terms.definition: A step-up elevation journey execution performed within this session after establishment. The session's effective AAL is the latest successful execution's (establishing or elevating); elevation freshness is a policy concern, not session structure.

terms.name: establishedBy
terms.definition: The authentication journey execution that established this session. Mandatory, exactly one (enforced in SHACL). Retargeted from AuthenticationEvent to AuthenticationJourneyExecution in 0.2.0, while draft.

terms.name: hasDeviceClass
terms.definition: Class of a device, from the closed device-class vocabulary.

terms.name: hasState
terms.definition: Current lifecycle state of the session.

terms.name: impliesChannel
terms.definition: Delivery channel a device class corroborates. The channel a session was served over is established by its journey definition; where a session also has a device, its class must imply the same channel.

terms.name: issuedToken
terms.definition: Token issued within this session.

terms.name: onDevice
terms.definition: Device the session runs on. At most one, and a principal may hold at most one active session per device (enforced in SHACL). Absent for non-interactive sessions.

terms.name: resolvesToSession
terms.definition: Session a presented handle identifies. Exactly one (enforced in SHACL) — a handle resolving to two sessions is a session-fixation hazard.

terms.name: tokenAudience
terms.definition: Resource for which a token is intended — the aud claim: who may accept the token.

terms.name: Gateway
terms.definition: A network entry point into the platform, exposing one or more listeners through which external traffic arrives.

constraints.message: A gateway must expose at least one listener.

terms.name: Listener
terms.definition: A protocol/port binding on a gateway.

constraints.message: A listener must have exactly one valid port.
Listener protocol must be one of HTTPS, TLS, TCP, HTTP.
Listener uses plaintext HTTP — confirm this is an internal redirect-only listener.

terms.name: Route
terms.label: Route
terms.definition: A rule mapping matched traffic on a gateway to an upstream service. A route that binds a tenant and serves an application is the addressable endpoint through which that application is entered: it carries the domain and path, the tenant binding, the mediating enforcement point, and a governed declaration behind the binding.

constraints.message: Route serves an application its bound tenant does not own — a cross-tenant endpoint.
Route serves an application at a scope outside that application's enablement — reachable where it is not enabled.
Route binds a tenant but declares no hostname — tenant context cannot be resolved from an address that is not stated.
Two routes bind the same domain and path to different tenants — one address must resolve to exactly one tenant.
Route binds a tenant with no route-binding declaration behind it — tenant resolution must be governed, not configured out of band.
A route must forward to at least one upstream service.
Every route must be mediated by exactly one policy enforcement point before its upstream.
A route binds at most one tenant, and what it binds must be a tenant — a domain resolves to a tenant, it does not substitute for one.
A route serves at most one application — an access endpoint addresses one application boundary.

terms.name: TLSConfiguration
terms.definition: TLS settings applied at a listener, including where TLS terminates relative to policy enforcement.

terms.name: UpstreamService
terms.definition: A backend service to which routes forward traffic.

terms.name: hostname
terms.definition: Domain a route matches. Together with the path prefix it forms the address a tenant is reached at; a tenant-bound route must carry one (enforced in SHACL).

terms.name: pathPrefix
terms.definition: Path prefix a route matches within its domain. Absent means the whole domain; present, it lets one domain serve several tenants or applications at different paths.

terms.name: port
terms.definition: Port number of a listener.

terms.name: protocol
terms.definition: Protocol of a listener (HTTPS, TLS, TCP).

terms.name: terminatesTLS
terms.definition: Whether TLS terminates at this listener (true) or is passed through (false).

terms.name: boundToTenant
terms.definition: Tenant that traffic matching this route resolves to. Ingress establishes tenant context from this binding, not from any token claim.

terms.name: exposesRoute
terms.definition: Route attached to a gateway or listener.

terms.name: hasListener
terms.definition: Listener exposed by a gateway.

terms.name: hasTLSConfiguration
terms.definition: TLS configuration applied to a listener.

terms.name: routesTo
terms.definition: Upstream service to which a route forwards traffic.

terms.name: servesApplication
terms.definition: Application reachable through this route. With the tenant binding, this makes the route the endpoint an application is entered at, so admission can ask whether a subject may enter THIS application through THIS endpoint rather than merely whether the tenant owns some enabled application.

terms.name: Action
terms.definition: An operation a policy decision evaluates — the action slot of the evaluation tuple. Members are individuals in a closed, platform-owned scheme.
terms.editorialNote: Application verbs such as transfer or approve belong to Level-3 application authorization and must never appear here.

vocabulary.label: Access
vocabulary.definition: Cross a platform or application boundary — the admission action.

vocabulary.label: Administer
vocabulary.definition: Mutate platform configuration or policy — control-plane operations.

terms.name: AttributeAssertion
terms.definition: A first-class attribute statement about a principal or resource: name, value, issuer, and validity window. Attributes carry provenance rather than being baked into role hierarchies.

constraints.message: An attribute assertion must have exactly one name.
An attribute assertion must have a value.
An attribute assertion must have an authoritative issuer — attributes without provenance cannot be used in decisions.
An attribute assertion must describe exactly one principal.

terms.name: DecisionOutcome
terms.definition: XACML decision outcome; members are individuals.

terms.name: EntitlementDimension
terms.definition: A coarse-grained access dimension ingress validates at the platform boundary. Members are individuals in a closed, platform-owned scheme; applications cannot introduce dimensions — extension is a deliberate MINOR-versioned act behind security-architecture review.

terms.name: EntitlementGrant
terms.definition: A conferral of platform access to a tenant on one entitlement dimension, with a value and validity window. Always a materialized projection of upstream governance, distributed to ingress.
terms.editorialNote: The token is evidence; the grant is authority.

constraints.message: An entitlement grant must confer access to exactly one tenant.
An entitlement grant must name exactly one dimension from the platform-owned scheme.
An entitlement grant must carry a derivation link to its governing source — hand-authored grants are forbidden; grants are projections.
Grant has no distribution timestamp — staleness queries cannot cover it.

terms.name: IngressAdmissionDecision
terms.definition: A decision at the ingress policy enforcement point admitting a request across a platform or application boundary: subject, action and target evaluated against distributed entitlement grants.
terms.editorialNote: Aligned to the AuthZEN evaluation tuple. The evaluated policy is the platform admission policy — the versioned unit of authorization logic the distributed grant configuration realizes.

constraints.message: An admission decision must arrive via exactly one channel, derived from the presenting registration.
An admission decision must evaluate at least one entitlement grant — admission without grants is admission without authority.
Admission decision evaluated a tenant's grants for a principal holding no active membership in that tenant.

terms.name: Obligation
terms.definition: An action the enforcement point must perform alongside enforcing a decision (log, step-up, watermark).

terms.name: Policy
terms.definition: A named, versioned unit of authorization logic governing one or more resources.

constraints.message: A policy must contain at least one rule.

terms.name: PolicyDecision
terms.definition: An evaluation of policy for a specific access request, with an outcome.

constraints.message: A policy decision must have exactly one outcome.
A policy decision must reference the policy it evaluated.
A policy decision must evaluate exactly one action — the AuthZEN tuple is incomplete without it.
A policy decision must name exactly one policy decision point — a decision nobody can be shown to have made is unattributable.
A policy decision must name the requesting principal — a decision with no subject cannot be traced to anyone (P17).
Decision evaluates an action outside the platform-owned action vocabulary — application verbs are Level-3 and must not reach platform decisions.
Permit decision violates policy assurance requirement: the session's authentication AAL is below the policy's required AAL.

terms.name: PolicyRule
terms.definition: A single rule within a policy, with an effect (permit/deny) and conditions over attributes.

constraints.message: A rule must have exactly one effect: 'permit' or 'deny'.

terms.name: Role
terms.definition: A named collection of permissions; retained for RBAC interop, but modelled as one source of attribute assertions among others.

terms.name: attributeName
terms.definition: Name of the asserted attribute (e.g., 'lineOfBusiness', 'clearance').

terms.name: attributeValue
terms.definition: Value of the asserted attribute.

terms.name: distributedAt
terms.definition: Instant this grant projection was last distributed to the enforcement point; anchors staleness queries.

terms.name: effect
terms.definition: Effect of a rule: 'permit' or 'deny'.

terms.name: entitlementValue
terms.definition: Value a grant confers on its dimension (e.g., 'US' on region, 'prod' on environment, 'web' on channel).

terms.name: aboutPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal an attribute assertion describes.

terms.name: assertedBy
terms.definition: Authoritative source (PIP, IdP, HR system) that issued an attribute assertion.

terms.name: decidedBy
terms.definition: Policy decision point that rendered this decision. Mandatory (SHACL): a decision nobody can be shown to have made is unattributable, and the platform and each application run their own decision point.

terms.name: decisionOutcome
terms.definition: Outcome concept of a policy decision.

terms.name: derivedFrom
terms.definition: Upstream governance object a grant was projected from: a subscription, an application enablement, or a route binding. Mandatory — a grant with no derivation is hand-authored.
terms.editorialNote: Platform, tenant and channel grants properly originate in the tenant onboarding record, which is not yet modelled.

terms.name: evaluatedAction
terms.definition: The action a policy decision evaluated — exactly one per decision (SHACL), drawn from the platform-owned action scheme. AuthZEN's action name is the concept's skos:notation.

terms.name: evaluatedGrant
terms.definition: Entitlement grant an admission decision evaluated.

terms.name: evaluatedPolicy
terms.definition: Policy evaluated to produce a decision.

terms.name: grantedTo
terms.definition: Tenant to which an entitlement grant confers access.

terms.name: hasRule
terms.definition: Rule contained in a policy.

terms.name: imposesObligation
terms.definition: Obligation attached to a rule or decision.

terms.name: onDimension
terms.definition: Entitlement dimension a grant confers access on; must be drawn from the platform-owned scheme.

terms.name: requestingPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal whose access request the decision concerns.

terms.name: requiredAssuranceLevel
terms.definition: Minimum AAL a policy requires of the session's originating authentication.

terms.name: viaChannel
terms.definition: Delivery channel through which an admission decision's request arrived, derived from the presenting registration.

terms.name: withinSession
terms.definition: Session in which the access request was made.

terms.name: AdministrativeScope
terms.definition: A bounded set of resources over which administrative authority is granted (tenant, namespace, line of business).

terms.name: ApplicationEnablement
terms.definition: A desired-state declaration enabling an application within the declaration's scope. terms.name: CapabilityBundle
terms.definition: A named set of capabilities offered for subscription together. Bundles are sales-time convenience: subscribing to one expands to per-capability subscriptions, materialized; enforcement and reachability never see bundles.

terms.definition: A control plane governing one platform capability, and the designated writer that actuates governed desired state into that capability's data planes.

terms.name: CapabilityRequirement

terms.definition: A desired-state declaration changing an authentication journey definition. Journey definitions are security-relevant desired state; this subclass gives their changes scope, approval rigor, and supersession through the standard declaration machinery.

terms.name: ManagementControlPlane
terms.definition: The control plane that owns the governance layer: tenant registration, entitlement configuration, and desired-state declarations. It defines; it never actuates a data plane (enforced in SHACL).
